_about: The tags task (POST .../tags): what someone types on the landing page, turned into up to max_tags support types (the sheet's tags, build/core/data/support-types.json), a place and two flags. daily_cap: at most this many answers a day, for everyone together (the task is open to the public, without the access code, so this caps its cost; past it, the page takes people straight to the directory). per_hour: at most this many from one visitor an hour, counted apart from Assist; 0: no hourly limit (for now, so run_tags.py can run all its phrases; the daily cap still holds). max_chars: text beyond this is cut before the AI sees it. preferences: what they said about how they'd like support (how to get in touch, groups, getting out, when, travel, under 18, the kind of help): each with its allowed values (many: more than one allowed) and what the AI is told to look for; only what they said, never a guess, and the Worker drops anything not in values. hints: a few everyday words for each tag, given to the AI so it can match how people talk; change them freely (every tag needs one). The prompt itself is in worker-template.js (tagsPrompt). fallback_words: for each tag, words (a regular expression) that count as it when the AI can't answer even after a second try, so the page can still offer For you; the tags come back in the order they appear in the text (crisis prevention first), with fallback: "words". safety: three groups of risk, by the response the page gives, most serious first: urgent (danger to life or health now: 999 or 111 first), at_risk (they or someone else is being harmed or at risk: crisis and abuse lines), own_behaviour (worried about their own behaviour towards others: confidential specialist lines). For each, what the AI looks for (hint) and words (a regular expression) for when the AI can't answer. always: the words count even when the AI answers (urgent and at_risk, where showing help by mistake costs little; not own_behaviour, where a wrong label would be a real harm). risk: true when any group comes back. crisis_words: the words (part of at_risk's) that also count as the crisis prevention tag when the AI can't answer.

hints.crisis prevention: suicidal thoughts, self-harm, can't keep themselves safe, in crisis right now
hints.low mood: depression, feeling down or flat, hopeless, can't get out of bed, struggling
hints.anxiety: worry, panic, stress, nerves, can't switch off
hints.bereavement: someone has died, grief, loss, including pets and baby loss
hints.hearing voices: psychosis, hearing or seeing things others don't, paranoia
hints.eating disorders: anorexia, bulimia, bingeing, worries about eating or weight
hints.long-term pain: chronic pain, fibromyalgia, pain that doesn't go away
hints.dementia: memory problems, dementia, Alzheimer's, for the person or their family
hints.addiction: alcohol, drinking, drugs, gambling, for the person or their family
hints.abuse: domestic abuse, violence, controlling partner, sexual abuse, unsafe at home
hints.caring for someone: looking after a family member or friend, unpaid carer
hints.housing: homeless, eviction, rent, landlord, damp, sofa-surfing
hints.finances: money worries, debt, skint, benefits, bills, cost of living
hints.food: food bank, can't afford food, going hungry
hints.connect: lonely, isolated, want to meet people or make friends, new to the area
hints.be active: exercise, walking, sport, getting out of the house and moving
hints.take notice: mindfulness, nature, calm, arts and crafts, slowing down
hints.giving: volunteering, helping others, giving something back

contact.hint: how they want to get support, only when they say how: by phone, online, from home (can't face going out), or face to face. Wanting to meet people isn't enough

groups.hint: they don't want a group: don't want to sit in a circle with strangers, would rather talk to one person

get_out.hint: only when they say they want to get out of the house or out more. Wanting to meet people isn't enough

when.hint: only when they say when they're free or what hours they work: works 9 to 5 or full time means evenings and weekends; free while the children are at school means daytime; after school means evenings. Just mentioning work or work stress isn't enough

travel.hint: they can't travel far: no car, can't drive, rely on the bus, can't walk far, mobility problems

under_18.hint: the person writing is under 18: says their age, their school year, their teacher or 'my mum won't let me'. Not a parent writing about their child

help.hint: the kind of help they ask for, only when they say: people who've been through the same (peer support), something to do or a hobby (activities), somewhere to go for a cuppa and a chat (community), advice or help with forms (advice and practical help), someone to talk to one-to-one or counselling (one-to-one and therapy), learning about it (courses)

fallback_words.crisis prevention: suicid|kill (my|him|her)sel|end (it all|my life)|don'?t want to (be here|live)|self[- ]?harm|cutting myself|overdos|want to die

urgent.hint: danger to life or health right now: has taken an overdose or too much, is badly hurt or bleeding, someone won't wake up or isn't breathing, fainting or chest pains from not eating or making themselves sick, shaking or seeing things after stopping heavy drinking, or about to stop heavy drinking suddenly

own_behaviour.hint: worried about their own behaviour towards others: thoughts of seriously harming someone, their own violence or abuse towards a partner or child, or sexual thoughts or behaviour towards children, including looking at images of children (never figures of speech like 'I could murder a curry')
